title: Kubernetes Confidential Containers Get Fortanix Attestation and Key Management
gist: Fortanix has added support for the CNCF's Confidential Containers (CoCo) to its Confidential AI platform. Its Confidential Computing Manager attests Kubernetes workloads running in TEEs, and its Data Security Manager releases keys to decrypt models and data only to environments that pass. The article notes that CoCo's open-source Trustee and Azure Secure Key Release already offer attestation-gated key release, and that attestation does not cover guest-software trust, side channels or whether an AI application handles data safely.

insights.claim: Fortanix's CoCo integration uses plugins to connect workloads to two services. Confidential Computing Manager (CCM) verifies the environment, and Data Security Manager (DSM) releases keys only to environments CCM has verified. If attestation fails, the keys stay in DSM and the workload cannot decrypt protected models or data.
insights.speaker: Mark Silvester
insights.so_what: Releasing keys only after attestation is how confidential AI protects model weights and sensitive data while they are in use.
insights.quote: keys stay in DSM if attestation fails, so the workload cannot decrypt protected models or data
insights.locator: CoCo moves image pulling and unpacking

insights.claim: Fortanix pitches combined attestation and key management as a way for teams to adopt standard CoCo without building the trust layer themselves. CCM and DSM run clustered, with 24x7 support, as a hosted service, on-premises or air-gapped.
insights.speaker: Anuj Jaiswal
insights.so_what: The vendor's value proposition is packaging and support around open-source CoCo.
insights.quote: With attestation and key management in one platform, teams can adopt standard CoCo without building the trust layer themselves.
insights.locator: Fortanix chief product officer Anuj Jaiswal

insights.claim: In Fortanix's Intel TDX guide, GPU attestation is a setting. Required makes CCM validate GPU evidence through NVIDIA's attestation service, while Ignored only checks that evidence is present and disregards the result. The Helm chart also does not configure host firmware or kernel settings.
insights.speaker: Mark Silvester
insights.so_what: The claim of joint CPU and GPU attestation holds only if operators choose the strict setting and prepare the hosts themselves.
insights.quote: Ignored checks only that evidence is present and disregards the result
insights.locator: Fortanix's Intel TDX deployment guide offers

insights.claim: CoCo support is available now. CCM's 17 September release notes added CoCo application registration for AMD SEV-SNP and Intel TDX. Fortanix says it is developing open-source plugins for CoCo but has not named repositories or versions.
insights.speaker: Mark Silvester
insights.so_what: The open-source commitment is not yet verifiable.
insights.locator: Fortanix says CoCo support is available

insights.claim: CoCo runs Kubernetes pods inside confidential VMs backed by hardware TEEs that encrypt memory and restrict access while the workload runs. This protects data in use, not just at rest or in transit, and lets sensitive workloads run on shared infrastructure.
insights.speaker: Mark Silvester
insights.so_what: Running sensitive AI workloads on shared cloud infrastructure becomes more viable.
insights.quote: This helps protect data in use, not just data at rest or in transit

insights.claim: CoCo's open-source Trustee components already provide attestation and conditional secret delivery. Trustee's attestation service compares platform claims with reference values, and its Key Broker Service applies a user-defined policy before releasing secrets. It also accepts GPU evidence bound to the processor's attestation report.
insights.speaker: Mark Silvester
insights.so_what: Fortanix's differentiation is operational packaging, not new capability.
insights.quote: Attestation and conditional secret delivery already exist in CoCo's open-source Trustee components.
insights.locator: Attestation and conditional secret delivery already

insights.claim: Microsoft's Azure Secure Key Release, in Key Vault Premium and Managed HSM and integrated with Azure Attestation, is a managed alternative. It releases exportable keys, not secrets or certificates.
insights.speaker: Mark Silvester
insights.so_what: Hyperscalers compete directly with Fortanix on attestation-gated key release.
insights.quote: It releases exportable keys, not secrets or certificates.
insights.locator: Microsoft's Azure Secure Key Release offers

insights.claim: The pod's guest kernel and helper processes sit inside the trust boundary and must be trusted. CoCo's trust model excludes denial-of-service protection and hardware side channels, and attestation does not show that an AI application handles data safely.
insights.speaker: Mark Silvester
insights.so_what: Confidential computing reduces risk from the host but does not guarantee application-level data safety.
insights.quote: Attestation does not establish that an AI application handles data safely.
insights.locator: The pod's guest kernel and helper
